description: Search WindowsForum threads with structured controls — sort by relevance, date, views or replies, in either order, with pagination; use when result ordering or paging matters. Latest/newest requests replace the default relevance sort with date order; a query such as 'latest tutorials' lists that section without requiring those words in the content. Views/replies sort the complete indexed matching corpus inside a frozen snapshot; they require a complete, fresh popularity index. Counts shown for these sorts come from that index snapshot, with a conservative counts_as_of freshness watermark. Ranking metadata identifies an applied database transaction barrier or a rolling metadata sweep. Native view totals are source-aggregated on approximately a 15-minute cadence, so recent visits and subsequent source changes may not yet be reflected. For popularity continuation pass next_cursor as cursor, leaving from_=0; cursors are short-lived (well under two minutes), so page promptly and start again from the first page if one has expired. The total is exact when total_relation is 'eq', otherwise a verified public lower bound ('gte'); use has_more and next_from to continue. If pagination_limited is true, narrow the query or section instead of paging further.

cursor.description: Popularity-only continuation token from next_cursor; reuse the same query, section and sort

from_.description: Continuation offset: the number of results already shown. Pass next_from from the previous page.

section.description: Part of the site to cover. Keep the default 'all' for questions and troubleshooting, so threads, news and tutorials all come back. Use 'threads', 'news' or 'tutorials' only when the user asks for that one kind of content, e.g. 'tutorials' for 'show tutorials'.

name: search_threads
title: Search threads (sortable)
